viz.cloudMethods:
Cloud Detection Methods

Clouds can be detected two ways on the cross-section:

  • NWP Layers — derived from the numerical weather prediction model's cloud cover parameterisation (low / mid / high bands). Shows where the model itself predicts clouds.
  • DD Layers — derived from dewpoint depression in the sounding profile. When the gap between temperature and dewpoint is small (DD < 2°C), air is near saturation and cloud is likely. This is a sounding-based signal independent of the model's cloud scheme.

Both methods can be enabled simultaneously for comparison. They often agree in moist layers but may differ where NWP sub-grid clouds or local moisture are present.
viz.convectionMethods:
Convective Methods

The cross-section offers two convective risk overlays:

  • Thermo — risk from thermodynamic indices (CAPE, CIN). Tower bounds from LFC/LCL (base) and EL (top). Zero risk when CAPE is zero, even if the NWP model parameterises convective clouds.
  • NWP — risk from the NWP model's native convective cloud parameterisation (GFS convective cover %). Tower bounds are model-computed convective base/top. This typically matches what GRAMET shows.

Enable both to compare. The advisory system uses whichever method you select in your profile settings.
viz.icingMethods:
Icing Methods

The cross-section offers three icing overlays, each combining an icing formula with a cloud detection method:

Formulas

  • Ogimet — continuous parabolic index peaking at −7°C. Maps temperature to an icing severity index across the 0 to −14°C range (layered) or 0 to −20°C (convective). Simple, well-proven in European GA.
  • SFIP — fuzzy-logic algorithm combining temperature, relative humidity, cloud liquid water, and vertical velocity via membership functions. More complex, uses direct NWP moisture data when available.

Cloud Signals

  • DD (dewpoint depression) — sounding-based. Uses a continuous cosine taper: full icing index at DD = 0, zero at DD ≥ 2°C. No NWP cloud data needed.
  • NWP (model cloud cover) — uses the NWP model's cloud cover percentage at each altitude. 50% cloud → 50% of icing index. This is the approach used by Autorouter GRAMET.

The Three Methods

  • Ogimet-DD — Ogimet formula + DD cloud signal
  • Ogimet-NWP — Ogimet formula + NWP cloud signal
  • SFIP-NWP — SFIP fuzzy-logic (inherently uses NWP moisture inputs)

Enable multiple methods to compare them side-by-side. The advisory system uses whichever method you select in your profile settings.

wizard.tourSubtitle: Here's how to get started with Flyfun Weather.
wizard.step1Desc: Enter your waypoints (airport ICAO codes), date and time. Your aircraft defaults are pre-filled from the profile you just set up.
wizard.step2Desc: The briefing opens automatically. It shows red/amber/green advisories, an AI synopsis, interactive cross-section, and sounding analysis for each waypoint.
wizard.step3Desc: Come back and refresh the briefing as the flight date approaches — each refresh captures a new snapshot you can compare. You can also set up an auto-refresh at a given time to receive an update by email each day.
wizard.step3Hint: Note: a refresh can take around 1 minute.
wizard.step4Desc: Use Compact mode for a summary or Full Details to explore every metric. Click on any point in the cross-section to see all metrics and Skew-T for all models. This can be used on the day of the flight but is most useful to form an early picture of the feasibility of a flight.
wizard.step5Desc: Click them anywhere in the briefing to learn what a metric means and how to interpret it.
wizard.tourHint: You can revisit these settings any time from the Settings page, and learn more on the Help page.
